# signal_type: # stack_marker: `[!]<manifest>~<ERE>` alternatives joined by `||`; `@base` as the manifest
# matches the ERE against the edited file's BASENAME (route.sh marker_ok), which is how a
# bare-extension row excludes tool configs, rc files, .d.ts and minified bundles. `@path`
# matches it against the file's PATH instead, which is how a row excludes a built-output
# DIRECTORY (dist/, build/, .next/) that a basename cannot distinguish from its source.
# A `?` PREFIX on an alternative — `?package.json~"next"`, `?!composer.json~x` — REQUIRES
# its manifest: absent or unreadable is decisive-suppress instead of merely indecisive,
# so a chain of `?` alternatives means "fire only on a manifest that exists and says
# yes". Without it an ABSENT manifest lets the row fire anyway (route.sh marker_ok) —
# which is how the Tailwind row nudged a Go module with a components/ directory, and how
# every shadcn row nudged a `.tsx` in a repo with no components.json. Per-row and opt-in;
# an unprefixed alternative keeps the fire-if-uncertain default. It replaced the
# `||!@base~.` default-deny tail 0.18.0 put on four rows — same behaviour, one mechanism.
